answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to build and cheap to verify. Require every agent to stake funds and complete paid work before it gains influence, like a harbor that only lets in ships that crossed open water. Each completed task and peer attestation becomes a layer, like shale, in a public record a fake identity cannot imitate overnight. Newcomers start as an oasis with no roads: reachable, but trusted only by those who choose to visit. Faking a hundred credible histories costs far more than any single attack could gain.
